notes: §1985:XII.2.4 GR4: "For purposes of matching, identifier-1, word-1, and literal-1 are treated as pseudo-text containing only identifier-1, word-1, or literal-1, respectively." ReadOperand returns a non-pseudo-text operand as the text-words it spans (the word, its OF/IN qualifiers and subscript separators, or the one literal), ParseReplacingOperands stores those as Replacement.From exactly as it stores the words of ==pseudo-text-1==, and ApplyReplacements compares them word by word through TextWord#MatchesForReplacing, so an operand matches only whole library text words. Witness 1985-GR-XII_2_4-4 (WS-A BY WS-B leaves WS-AX: NEWBX). Probes (work-rd-06/p): d) p4a A1 OF B1 replaces A1 OF B1 but not A1 IN B1 (character for character), T (1) matches T(1), ws-a in the library is matched by WS-A, +1 BY 9 replaces +1 and not 1, p3d 01 does not match 1 and "OLD" does not match "old"; b) p3r COPY as word-1 refused COBOL7006 (§1985:XII.2.3 SR6), a missing operand or BY COBOL2449; c) p3e partial-word phrases refused COBOL0900; a) the continued literal in L4A is one text word and is not matched by a shorter literal-1. The two identifier shapes ReadOperand cannot read (subscript plus reference modifier, function-identifier) are refused before matching; that defect is recorded under 1985-GR-XII.2.4-3. || REFUTED: PARTIAL - harm rejects-legal-source, one defect with 1985-GR-XII.2.4-3 (no separate note): ReadOperand reads a word, OF/IN qualifiers and one parenthesised group, so identifier-1 = data-name subscripted AND reference-modified, or a function-identifier (Amendment 1), is refused COBOL2449 instead of being matched as pseudo-text. next.reason: 1985 GR4 treats identifier-1, word-1 and literal-1 REPLACING operands as pseudo-text for matching. The 2023 COPY format (§2023:7.2.3.2, rendered PDF p.76) has no identifier, word or literal operand, and §2023:7.2.3.4 GR8 replaces only pseudo-text-1 or partial-word-1, so no 2023 rule carries this. The stray 'word-2, or literal-4' in §2023:7.2.3.4 GR9 has no syntax behind it.
